Hi Stephanie,

We're close to finalizing the procurement with our reseller partner (NorthStar Resale) and they asked for clarity on two items before we sign the private offer:

1) Commission / passback: what level of passback % does Redwood typically accept on Azure private offers where a reseller is the transacting party? NorthStar is asking for guidance so they can model their margin.
2) Tax handling: should the list price floor in the private offer include taxes (VAT/GST) or be listed net and let taxes be handled at invoice time? They want to know whether taxes are grossed-up for partner commission calculations.

If you can point us to the recommended approach and any sample wording we should include (or a template), that would help us move the PO along.

Thanks Steph — summary + recommendation below. Kept it concise so we can feed back to CloudLane.

Context / quick primer:
- Marketplace private offers (Azure) can list a list-price floor that the private offer will honor. Taxes (VAT/GST) are commonly handled at invoice time by the reseller in their market.
- Partner commission/passback is usually calculated on the net software value (list price excluding sales tax) in most reseller agreements. Grossing up for tax is rare and creates complexity for settlement.

Two pragmatic pathways (pros/cons):

Path A — List price floor = net software price; commission computed on net price (recommended default)
- Passback range: 8% — 12% for channel-first resellers on Azure private offers (10% is a good anchor).
- Pros: simple settlements, aligns with how our billing/tax engine treats transacted revenue; easier for finance.
- Cons: reseller bears tax collection/remittance; if they expect tax to be included in their margin calc, they need to gross-up locally.

Path B — List price floor includes estimated taxes; commission computed on gross price (less common)
- Passback range: set lower (6% — 9%) if you insist on gross commission to keep our net revenue target intact.
- Pros: easier for resellers who quote customers all-in; less need for local gross-up math.
- Cons: complicated to keep accurate across jurisdictions and creates reconciliation burden.

Operational notes / contract language to include:
- Private offer should explicitly state: "List price floor is stated net of applicable sales taxes; taxes to be collected/ remitted by the reseller in the customer's jurisdiction."
- Alternatively, if reseller insists on tax-inclusive listing, add a settlement clause: "Partner commission calculated on net software consideration; parties will reconcile tax variances within 60 days of invoice."

Recommendation: Tell CloudLane we prefer Path A (net list price) with a 10% passback for NorthStar Resale. Offer Path B only if they can accept a lower passback and agree to a 60-day reconciliation window.

I've attached a simple calc workbook that shows the impact on net revenue and partner take for a couple of scenarios. Ben: if this aligns, can you confirm we can operationalize 10% passback for Azure PO flows? Laura: can you flag any contract language tweaks needed for the private offer template?

-Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Hi Amir — thanks for the clear ask and apologies for the short turnaround.

We reviewed with RevOps and Contracts. Proposed next steps:

1) Recommended approach: List price floor should be stated net of taxes. Partner commission / passback should be calculated on the net software amount. Our recommended passback to NorthStar is 10%.

2) If NorthStar requires an all-in (tax-inclusive) listed price, we can accommodate but would request a lower passback (6–8%) plus a 60-day reconciliation clause to handle jurisdictional tax variance.

3) Tech/ops: Ben confirmed we can configure the Azure private offer flow to reflect net list price and passback at settlement. Laura will add the following clause to the private offer template: 

"List price floor is exclusive of applicable sales taxes. Partner commission is calculated on the net software consideration. Parties agree to reconcile any tax variances within 60 days of invoice issuance."

I attached the channels calc and a private offer template for your legal team. If that works for CloudLane, we can prepare the private offer in DocuSign this week and aim to have signatures in the next 3 business days.

Link to draft private offer: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/XYZ-PRIVATE-OFFER
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/87421
